content.text: Infection of the GI tract associated w/ vomiting & diarrhea
>3 episodes of loose/watery stools per day
– poultry, unpasteurized milk, untreated water, new pets, dairy farms
: mild diarrhea – pseudomembranous colitis – toxic megacolon
– beef, greens, unpasteurized milk, petting zoos, person-person
– poultry/beef, dairy, contaminated water, reptiles/amphibians, MC <4yo
– humans are only hosts; resource-limited settings
– infection requires low inoculum; childcare outbreaks
– SWINE; pork, milk, well water, chitterlings, tofu; uncommon in US
: generally begins w/ vomiting followed by
: sudden onset vomiting, watery diarrhea, abdominal pain, fever
: diarrhea w/ blood/mucus, abdominal pain, fever, systemic toxicity
w/ bloody diarrhea appearing 3-4d after sxs onset;
: initially – fever, malaise, myalgias, abdominal pain, constipation or bloody diarrhea; then –
: varies; watery stools w/o other sxs – bloody stools + high fever, abdominal pain, tenesmus
: fever, abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea in young children
: mesenteric lymphadenitis w/ fever, abdominal pain/tenderness, leukocytosis – older children
– gradual onset bloody diarrhea, lower abd. pain, tenesmus, wt loss;
: PCR; stool antigen tests have lower s/s
: culture using selective media (preferred), EIA, PCR
w/ confirmatory toxin testing by NAAT or toxin immunoassay
: culture on sorbitol containing selective media, EIA for Shiga toxin –
: blood culture, bile culture, bone marrow aspirate
; azithromycin x3d or erythromycin x5d can shorten duration when given early in illness
vancomycin 40mg/kg/d divided 4x daily x10d if severe
abx not recommended d/t HUS risk
: azithromycin or cipro x3d may ↓ duration
only in pts @ high risk of invasive disease
; then definitive therapy based on cultures x7-14d
•steroids may be beneficial in children w/ enteric fever (delirium, coma, shock)
: single dose doxy or azithromycin; erythromycin, cipro, or tetracycline x3d
gen ceph, Bactrim, aminoglycosides, FQs, tetracycline, doxy, chloramphenicol – only for neonates/IC
